title: Native centre sharing: zero first transcript, later query 1/4
head: 5efcbb6058d27aa8b988db8f18c7b678166b2783
body:
## Result

**Scoped native counterexample; no new supplier or κ.** Answers open question 3
of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2199, head
`30ec048eedcaca970f94bbec0fdd3c52eacf9fdc`.

The scalar D-only identity `backward1 centre = forward0 centre / 4` does not
lift to the actual cover-owner action for selected replica 0, calls 0 and 4.
The counterexample rules out more than identical raw carriers:

- At physical cover `g=rho_1(port0)`, put payload-constant D-field differences
  `(1,-1,-1,-1)` on ports `(0,1,6,7)`; all other differences are zero.
- **All eight first-call centre fields vanish on the entire cover**, before
  and after transport. The complete first native word leaves those four
  constants on D and adds them to T, with zero helper/private differences.
- At the later common owner `I`, the actual stage-1 routes expose only port0.
  Its channel-0 native input is exactly `1/4`; the post-transport amplitude at
  address 0 is `i/4`, and inverse carrier normalization returns `1/4`.

Thus no linear decoder of those eight saved full-cover fields alone, even
with arbitrary owner mixing and native transport, recovers this later query.
This is **not** a recursive-call tariff, a full native rank calculation, an
exclusion of additional observations/changed contracts, or an output-quotient
bound for overlapping scatters.

## Scope and evidence

Adds only `research/selected-centre-quarter-native/` (seven files).
The README gives the explicit eight-by-four column relation and kernel proof.
Each local orientation's **24,767 literal events** is executed with unpacked
exact Gaussian-dyadic statevectors on 512 local addresses, retaining native
children, residual/endpoint adapters, scalar signs and private clears.

The payload is constant on all 73 physical axes/tensor/spectator factors at
one cover owner; it is not an address-basis column. A legal restricted input
can falsify an all-input identity. No equality is inferred from constant-input
tests. Distinct arbitrary cover-owner arrays are retained, never identified.
Initial target/helper dirt is the same arbitrary baseline in both executions;
linearity justifies zero differences without assuming clean workspace.

Actual stage-0/1 owner/chart/translation recipes are bound and reconstructed.
Calls 1–3 touch none of the live witness families, and the first five scheduled
events are local sweeps, so no bridge or idle event is silently dropped.
Both complete local endpoints and pre/post carrier values are checked.

Positive controls reproduce [PR 2199](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2199)'s scalar quarter-factor on all 8×112 D
coefficients and the cancellation on cover-invariant inputs. Seven elementary
controls cover exact roots, phases, inverses and typed receipts. Four native
controls cover the cover-invariant case, wrong owner location, wrong backward
global phase and wrong gather coefficient. CLI tests generate a fresh receipt
and reject corrupted/wrong-typed responses under `-I -O -B`.

No native executor code is imported from pending PRs. The pinned Clifford
kernel supplies canonical circuits only for inverse normalization; the literal
word evaluator is new code with the retained conventions. Six selected archive
members are hashed before decoding, using unique full paths. Source Git blobs,
digests, all 73 columns of `g`, route digests and responses are retained.
No dependency installation, frozen-source edit or selected-record change.

Separate read-only AI review independently reconstructed the four-column
relation and all four 73-column routes without importing this verifier, and
obtained `1/4` from a separate backward causal-slice replay. A separate packed
evaluator checked the used centre transport and eight active endpoint adapters
on all 512 columns, phase included. No critical or important defect was found.
The review requested an explicit coordinate-covariance argument for the
nonconstant intermediate states at owner `g`; the README now includes it.
The global lift uses the retained native local-view embedding, not a newly
rebuilt physical address/stream compiler.

claimed. No full cold replay, global hosting/stream/compiler/precision invoice,
outer proof, supplier adoption or κ change. All inherited obligations remain.

The prescribed ceiling and ideal lever table were replayed: baseline
`a_cap≈0.001690054109089`, ideal two-call sharing about 1.90×. These are prior
planning numbers. This contribution removes no centre/copy/restoration charge
and proposes no changed moment. Any repair still owes additional information,
storage/transport, hosting, restoration, precision and a complete invoice.
